transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling really low most days. I wake up with this gray weight on me, and it doesn’t really go away. Even at work with the crew or when I’m around my kids, I just feel hollow, like I’m only going through the motions.
How long have you been feeling this way—days, weeks, or longer?
About three years now—three years and a few months. It started when the groundskeeping contract changed and our schedule got longer. Since then, it’s felt like work just took over my life.
During these past three years, have you ever had a stretch of days where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, different from your normal mood?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I don’t really have periods where I’m unusually up or full of energy.
During these past three years, have there been any stretches of two months or more where your mood felt back to normal, or has the low mood been continuous the whole time?
No, I can’t think of any stretch that long where I felt back to normal. It’s been there pretty much continuously since the schedule changed—about three years and three months now.

Over these past three years, have there been times when your low mood became noticeably worse or more intense than your usual baseline—for example, with much deeper sadness, loss of interest in almost everything, or trouble functioning—lasting at least two weeks, compared to how you feel most of the time?
I’m not sure what you mean by worse than the usual. It’s been low for so long that it all kind of runs together.

Right now, are you experiencing things like a near-total loss of interest or pleasure in activities, significant changes in your sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness—several of these together, nearly every day?

Yeah... it’s affecting me a lot. I’ve been missing details when I’m planning jobs and getting behind on the crew paperwork. And I’ve stopped going to the community garden and the music gatherings I used to help organize. Other people have had to take over things they used to count on me for.

How long have you been noticing this particular stretch of losing interest in the garden and music gatherings, along with the trouble concentrating at work—has it been at least two weeks straight, or does it come and go?

It’s been steady, not really coming and going. I keep missing things when I’m planning jobs, the paperwork piles up, and I’ve just been avoiding the garden and the music gatherings. Other people have had to step in for things I used to handle.

Has this level of severe symptoms—losing interest in the garden and music, and the trouble concentrating at work—been present the whole three years, or did it start or get noticeably worse more recently, like in the past few weeks or months?
It’s been like this for about three years and three months. It started when the groundskeeping contract changed our schedule—longer days—and it just kind of took over my life.
Along with the low mood and loss of interest, have you also noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, feeling unusually tired, or feeling worthless or guilty nearly every day during this time?

Yeah, I’m tired pretty much every day. By midmorning, it feels like I’ve already worked a full day. Even if I sleep on Sunday, I’m still dragging through basic stuff—loading tools, looking over job plans, even making dinner.
During this time, have you often felt worthless, or found yourself feeling excessively guilty about things, nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve been struggling, but I can’t say I’ve noticed feeling worthless or especially guilty nearly every day.
During this time, have you noticed a change in your sleep—like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a real change in my sleep, at least not nearly every day.
During this time, have you noticed a change in your appetite or your weight—either eating much more or much less than usual, or gaining or losing weight—nearly every day?
I can’t really say I’ve noticed much change in my appetite or weight, not on a regular basis anyway.
